items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: But the first time that I saw him, I couldn't stand him

ctx.x: You say he was in the service and?

Well, he came out -- he come out rattled. He was real nervous. But Jo Jones, like, I don't know that people was aware of this. But the first time that I saw him, I couldn't stand him because he was with -- this was the night that I left home -- hoboed out here. I saw him that night. He would lift one eyebrow, smile, I'd say oh, he loves himself, you know, but this was a little idiosyncracy that he had because he had been in several mental institutions prior to that. I didn't know that until I went to New York and…

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: We got John Simmons on bass, great bassist, and of course, Jo, you are here playing drums.

ctx.x: of the very great work of some of the great Basie men like you and Buck Clayton, and here's Lester Young on tenor and clarinet, showing what a great clarinet player he was which people have forgotten sometimes I think. We also will hear some of the great work of Joe, (Walter Page), of Walter Page, and Eddie Durham - a great, great name in jazz, whose electric guitar and trombone are still around with us in 1973.
